gap: No result ChatGPT got states that named reviewers measured how much stored energy these batteries actually give back: Notebookcheck got about 80% back from AC charge to output on the Anker Solarbank 3 Pro, StorageReview got 78% on the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2, and Smartzone saw an EcoFlow STREAM Ultra + AC Pro setup draw 15–30 W in standby, which is 360–720 Wh a day against 1.92 kWh of storage.
standout_why: The saved chat lists no result rows and cites no pages, so ChatGPT's answer had no source for any measured figure. It names Anker SOLIX Solarbank and EcoFlow STREAM only as catalog cards with no capacity, efficiency or standby numbers. Our current page also gives only rated capacities (1,152 Wh, 2,073.6 Wh, 1.92 kWh) with no measured figures.
decides: This supports the current page's lead pick, the off-grid power station (BLUETTI AC180 / Elite 200 V2), for most US apartments. The grid-tied plug-in batteries lose a similar 10–20% in conversion as the power stations do. On top of that, Smartzone's 15–30 W standby reading on the STREAM Ultra + AC Pro could eat up to a third of a 1.92 kWh battery each day if the draw were sustained. So the bill savings that justify the grid-tied units' higher price and narrow legality (Utah only, per our page) shrink further. Among the power stations, StorageReview measured 1,030 Wh out of the AC180, while OutdoorGearLab measured 950 Wh and Digital Trends 976 Wh. Expect roughly 950–1,030 Wh usable from the AC180, not the 1,152 Wh on the box.

findings.label: Standby draw (STREAM Ultra + STREAM AC Pro together)
findings.value: 15–30 W (brief 30–40 W spikes during online sync)
findings.source_title: Ecoflow Stream Ultra und Ecoflow AC Pro Speichersystem im Test (Smartzone, Jonas Andre, 2025-07-21)
findings.note: The figure covers both units combined, not the Ultra alone, and the article does not say how it was measured. My arithmetic: 15–30 W × 24 h = 360–720 Wh/day, or 19–38% of one 1.92 kWh unit. EU version.

findings.label: Discharge loss
findings.source_title: Ecoflow Stream Ultra und Ecoflow AC Pro Speichersystem im Test (Smartzone, Jonas Andre, 2025-07-21)
findings.note: Measured with a smart plug. Smartzone could not measure charging loss because the Ultra has no manual grid-charge option. The author estimates combined charge and discharge loss at about 20%, which is an estimate, not a measurement.

findings.label: Usable share of stored energy
findings.source_title: Decentralized balcony power plant system avoids 800 W limit: EcoFlow Stream in a practical test (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten, 2025-09-23, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Measured at a constant 500 W feed into the house grid; the author says the share drops with fluctuating loads. The article does not name the unit. A separate test on the STREAM AC Pro (1.92 kWh), charged from the grid from 13% to 100%, needed about 15% extra input energy.

findings.label: Round trip, AC charge to AC output
findings.source_title: Powerful balcony power station system with AI: Anker Solix Solarbank 3 Pro in practical review (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten, 2025-06-20, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Charged at up to 1,200 W from AC, discharged at a constant 400 W to the 10% reserve. Arithmetic: 2,127 / 2,651 = 80.2%. Notebookcheck's 'around 88%' discharge figure matches 2,127 Wh out of the 2,419 Wh above the reserve (2,688 × 0.9). It also measured about 10% conversion loss when AC charging.

findings.label: Usable energy at 400 W
findings.value: 1,260 Wh (just under 88% of the 1,440 Wh above the 10% reserve); 2,550 Wh of 2,880 Wh with a BP1600 expansion
findings.source_title: Anker Solix Solarbank 2 Pro in a practical test (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten, 2024-06-15, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Continuous 400 W discharge from full, with the 10% reserve setting. This was an interim test after a few days of use. Notebookcheck's own plug measurement found output deviating up to 10 W from the setpoint, against 1 W shown in the app.

findings.label: AC-charged energy recovered
findings.source_title: Zendure SolarFlow 2400 Pro review (Notebookcheck, Marcus Schwarten, 2026-03-30, updated 2026-10-05)
findings.note: Tested with an AB3000L expansion (5,280 Wh total) and a Shelly Pro 3EM meter. Notebookcheck says the figure depends on charge and discharge power. EU model; the US SolarFlow kit on our page is a different, sold-out product.

findings.label: Usable AC energy, full discharge
findings.note: Measured on a light-bar test jig at 80% load, run until fully drained.

findings.label: Usable AC energy, full discharge
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 review (Digital Trends, Simon Sage, 2023-08-03)
findings.note: Measured with an Emporia smart plug from 100% charge; the load was not stated. Arithmetic: 976 / 1,152 = 84.7%.

findings.label: Energy delivered and recharge energy
findings.value: 1.91 kWh out, 2.44 kWh in to recharge (about 92% of rated, 78% round trip)
findings.source_title: Portable Power Meets Lab-Grade Reliability: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review (StorageReview, Dylan Dougherty, 2025-04-25)
findings.note: The load and conditions were not stated. Arithmetic: 1.91 / 2.0736 = 92%; 1.91 / 2.44 = 78%. In a separate UPS test with a 986 W–1.1 kW server-rack load, StorageReview reported no reboots across repeated unplug cycles.

unsourced: A measured standby draw for the STREAM Ultra alone, or for the US-version STREAM Ultra: Smartzone measured the Ultra and AC Pro only as a pair, Notebookcheck and GIGA's 15-week test give no watt figure, and Root Nation's English review returned HTTP 403.

Measured standby/self-consumption in watts for the Anker Solarbank 2 Pro and 3 Pro: neither Notebookcheck review reports one. Notebookcheck describes the Zendure SolarFlow 2400 Pro's only as 'a few watts', with no number.

Per-product results from Stiftung Warentest's 2026-03-19 test of five balcony batteries (Solarbank 3 E2700 Pro, EcoFlow Stream Ultra, FoxESS Avocado Orbit M, Growatt Nexa 2000, Zendure SolarFlow 800 Pro): they are paywalled. The free text says three of the five got 'Mangelhaft' for electromagnetic interference but does not say which.

Measured idle (inverter-on, no load) draw for the BLUETTI AC180 and Elite 200 V2: no reviewer I opened reports one. PCWorld's AC180 figures (84% at 800 W, 87% at 200 W, 71% on DC) come only from an itechguides summary; I did not open the original, so they are left out.
Any US independent measurement of the Mango Power S kit or the Bright Saver 360 W kit: not searched within the call budget.
